what: SiTime replaces quartz crystals with silicon. Nearly every electronic device needs a timing reference, and SiTime makes silicon chips that do that job more accurately and more robustly than the quartz pieces they replace.
customers: Makers of data centre equipment, phones, cars, aerospace systems and industrial electronics.
money: silicon oscillators, resonators and clock chips
moat: A silicon timing technology nobody else has commercialised at scale, protected by patents and by the difficulty of matching quartz accuracy in silicon.
risks: 405 times earnings and 18 times sales: the price assumes years of flawless execution
Revenue collapsed from $284M to $144M in 2023 when customers cut inventory, so it is far from stable
Only $17M of cash, which is thin for a company at this valuation
opportunities: Revenue recovered from $144M to $327M in two years and is running at $683M over the last twelve months
Analysts see about 76% upside, with 12 covering the stock
AI data centres need far more precise timing than earlier equipment, which is the market it was built for
watch: Revenue growth from data centre customers and the gross margin.
